def fruit_distribution(s,n):
    
    lis = list()
    for i in s.split(' '):
        if i.isdigit():
            lis.append(int(i))
    return n - sum(lis)

# Unit test for function fruit_distribution
def test_fruit_distribution():
    # Test with typical input
    assert fruit_distribution("5 apples and 6 oranges", 19) == 8
    assert fruit_distribution("0 apples and 1 oranges", 3) == 2
    assert fruit_distribution("2 apples and 3 oranges", 100) == 95
    assert fruit_distribution("100 apples and 1 oranges", 120) == 19

    # Test with more complex strings
    assert fruit_distribution("10 apples and 20 oranges and 5 mangoes", 40) == 5
    assert fruit_distribution("1 apple and 1 orange and 1 banana", 10) == 7

    # Test with no digits in string
    assert fruit_distribution("apples and oranges", 10) == 10

    # Test with only digits
    assert fruit_distribution("3 4 5", 15) == 3

    # Test with zero distribution
    assert fruit_distribution("5 apples and 5 oranges", 10) == 0

    # Test with large numbers
    assert fruit_distribution("1000 apples and 2000 oranges", 5000) == 2000

    # Test with single item
    assert fruit_distribution("7 apples", 10) == 3

    # Test edge case: empty string
    assert fruit_distribution("", 5) == 5

    # Test with zero count
    assert fruit_distribution("0 apples and 0 oranges", 0) == 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_fruit_distribution()
    print("All tests passed!")
